## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results in this search yet, and generation 0 scored 0 in all 84 trials. Training success was also 0, so the agent never learned at all, whatever the network or recipe. One possible cause no earlier idea targeted is when to stop. Success needs DONE at exactly the right step. A random policy picks DONE with chance of about 1/150 per step, so it rarely tries DONE on a finished build and never gets the +1. After that point, every extra brick only spoils the build. In a hierarchical stop-or-place parameterisation, the DONE logit becomes a learned stop logit plus logsumexp of the placement logits. That makes the stop choice a cheap binary decision with a reasonable starting rate, so stopping gets explored early. Separately, I test recipe settings no earlier trial used: lr 3e-3, n_envs above 256, gae_lambda 0.8 and gamma 0.99. One candidate combines both changes, to raise the chance of seeing any nonzero signal.

### Round 2
Round 1 gave 0.000 on every seed again, so 87 trials in total have scored zero on dev and in training. Network families, recipes and DONE parametrisations do not seem to matter. This points to a failure common to every file, and probably one tied to how this world differs from its description. Two candidates fit and have never been tested. First, scale: if some observation channel or the reward has an unexpected magnitude, unnormalised inputs saturate the network. Second, the fixed global gradient-norm clip of 1.0: if the critic's gradients dominate the total norm, clipping shrinks the policy gradient to almost nothing. This was possible even with the earlier separate critic. Adam's step size does not depend on gradient scale, so scaling down the critic's gradients keeps its learning speed but stops it dominating the clip. This round tests each fix alone, then both together with hierarchical DONE and longer-horizon credit assignment.

### Round 3
After 90 trials, every one has scored 0 on dev and 0 in training, on both seeds. Seed noise cannot be measured and no idea can be ranked. In this round, six changes all scored 0: a fast recipe with large batches and lambda 0.8, a hierarchical DONE, input scale robustness with GroupNorm, critic gradient scaling, and two combinations. So a hidden input scale, value gradients dominating the clip, and DONE exploration on their own are unlikely to be the cause. An exact build needs every placement right and then a DONE at exactly the right moment. With only about 4,000 to 13,000 episodes of budget, the likely bottleneck is sample efficiency and credit for the +1 bonus. Untried directions: near-Monte-Carlo credit (gamma 0.995, lambda 0.99, full-episode rollouts), a type-then-cell factorised policy, and the standard PPO initialisation (orthogonal weights, 0.01 policy-output gain).

### Round 4
All 9 trials in this search scored 0.000 on both seeds, with 0 training success. The same was true for all 84 trials in generation 0. That is a large, consistent null result. These changes did not unblock learning: recipe tweaks, hierarchical DONE, input normalisation, critic gradient scaling, factorised type-then-cell heads and orthogonal init. A network bug is unlikely, because dense, layout-free and many structured heads all fail in the same way. The likelier causes are a world-level difference or a budget too small for exact builds to ever happen. With no nonzero signal, seed noise is unknown. Untried regions remain: lr 3e-3 combined with the maximum sample count (ppo_epochs 1), much smaller networks, and constant coordinate channels. This last round spends its three trials there, since even a single nonzero seed would beat the starting architecture.
